correctness.rationale: Eliminating steady-state R,C yields F(I)=I+alpha I N(I)/D(I)=1−(mu+alpha)/beta with N linear and D quadratic in I. The quotient derivative numerator n0d0+2n1d0 I+(n1d1−n0d2)I² has strictly positive coefficients; the source factorization Q>0 works for independently varying epsilons and 0<=sigma<=1. Unique root 0<I<L reconstructs a strictly positive simplex state; fixed-I parameter derivatives yield strict epsilon1 and conditional epsilon2 monotonicity, equality at sigma=1. The uniform positive lower bound on I makes a,b grow when respective feedbacks diverge, establishing the two distinct one-axis rational limiting equations and the joint I->L with immune states vanishing. The inspected SymPy checker tests algebraic identities, a finite example and boundaries, not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: No claim about stability, equilibria in the subcritical regime beyond disease free, or transmission-driven feedback.

value.rationale: The global all-strength uniqueness and comparative-statistics classification already exists with the same exact formula and stronger scope in the October 11 record. The remaining two one-axis limits arise immediately by coefficient comparison in those already published rational formulas, without a new structural lemma or independently motivated unsolved parameter invariant. Correctness and a worked example do not make this duplicated global theorem an original worthwhile contribution. No narrowed corrected full science package was developed, so rejecting the unchanged original is appropriate.
residual_risks: One-axis limits are mathematically interpretable epidemiologically, but insufficient here to overcome a dominating prior theorem.
